title: Regional Chair governance opposition and data centre study
subtitle: Also: Wrigley Road safety, lab expansion tender, Victoria Street reconstruction, overnight accessible taxis, transit gaps, tariff procurement analysis.
overview: Regional Council opposed any model that lets one person serve as both a mayor and Regional Chair, and voiced concern about combining strong mayor and strong chair powers. The resolution goes to the Premier, the housing minister, local MPPs and municipalities {{vote:m13}}. A provision about separating municipal and regional leadership was removed first.

Council also asked staff for an information report on data centres, due in early 2027, covering water, electricity, cost and environmental effects. Staff will also look at gaps in transit coverage and at penalties or incentives for bus stop snow clearing. Council approved a $25.1 million lab expansion tender and a Victoria Street South reconstruction tender, and continued two overnight accessible taxis.

After hearing from North Dumfries residents about Wrigley Road, council directed staff to look at speeding up the traffic calming study. Council also asked staff to analyze how tariffs affect Regional procurement. Closed session covered legal advice and labour matters; the minutes report no decisions from it.

decisions.item: Opposing combined mayor and Regional Chair roles
decisions.detail: Council opposed one person serving as both mayor and Regional Chair, expressed concern about concentrated strong mayor and strong chair powers, and will send the resolution to the province and municipalities.
Staff will prepare an information report on data centre impacts, including infrastructure, water, environment, finances and possible provincial advocacy, and report back by Q1 2027.

decisions.item: Transit gaps and bus stop snow clearing
decisions.detail: Staff will identify short-term transit connectivity gaps and report before the 2027 Budget, and explore penalties or incentives and easier public reporting for missed bus stop snow clearing.
The Region will continue two on-call accessible taxis between 11:00 PM and 5:00 AM after the 2026 pilot showed rising demand.
Council accepted Magil Construction Canada Inc.'s tender of $25,137,759 plus taxes for the Region of Waterloo lab expansion.
Council accepted a $10,230,047.10 tender from T. Musselman Excavating for reconstructing Regional Road 55 in Kitchener, with cost increases for City of Kitchener and Bell Canada work at no net cost.
Council approved how speed camera net revenues and provincial Road Safety Initiatives Fund money will be shared with partner municipalities, and authorized a Round 2 provincial application.
Council approved an exemption allowing Victoria Park Community Homes to carry more than ninety percent encumbrance on one Cambridge property.

debate: A North Dumfries delegate and a township councillor asked for a lower speed limit through the Wrigley settlement, now 80 km/h, and a corridor-wide safety study. They cited no sidewalks or lighting, residents crossing the road for mail, a recent serious pedestrian collision, and growth from new housing and gravel pits.

Staff said a township traffic calming program is studying 47 sites, including Wrigley Road, with measures expected mid next year. Council asked staff to see whether that could be sped up, and staff said yes.

A delegate on data centres urged the report to categorize them by size and purpose, include public feedback, and look at effects on the whole electricity grid. Staff said the report is a starting point and may raise more questions than it answers.

On the Regional Chair motion, supporters raised impartiality, conflicts of interest, concentrated authority and the time demands of two full-time roles. Two councillors questioned the provision on separating municipal and regional leadership, and the mover agreed to strike it.
One councillor suggested asking the province to let the next council choose the Chair as a middle ground. Another said residents are raising the issue at the doors.
